newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to consider UES convertible bond decree.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to consider UES convertible bond decree.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov will on Wednesday present President Boris Yeltsin with a draft decree allowing the issue of convertible bonds by national power utility UES, Russian news agencies said.

They said the decree on the bonds, which are expected to hit international markets this autumn, would raise five trillion roubles ($870 million) intended to pay wage arrears. It needs Yeltsin's signature to come into force.
"Boris Nemtsov will present the head of state draft decrees (including) issue of bonds by RAO UES," Itar-Tass news agency said. The presidential press service was unable to confirm the comments.

Government and UES officials have said the decree will spell out the size of the convertible bond issue, which could cover 1.5-5.0 percent of company shares, including up to 2.7 percent minus one share of the government's 52.7 percent stake.

Unissued authorised shares controlled by UES may also be used in the programme, which is expected to be preceded by an American Depositary Receipt programme to allow overseas trading of UES shares and increase UES their liquidity and price.

UES is Russia's largest company by sales and assets with controlling stakes in most power utilities and its share price was $0.4174 at the close of the Russian Trading System on Tuesday compared with about $0.08 last December.
